title: Secret Project or Death Trap?
captions: My new manager announced a “secret project” that will give the winner a promotion—if they survive the week. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #office #challenge
Day two of the live‑streamed nightmare. Who will crack the next clue before the clock runs out? #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #office #survival
The final room reveals everything. Was I right to sabotage? Tell me your verdict. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #office #ethics
parts: [[DAY 1 · 09:00 AM]] My new manager announced a “secret project” that will give the winner a promotion—if they survive the week. [[RULE 1 · NO HELP]] He flashes a grin, then slides a sleek tablet across the table. "All tasks are live‑streamed. No one leaves until the end." The room hums. My heart pounds. I glance at my coworkers; their faces are tight, eyes flickering between curiosity and dread. [[COUNTDOWN 5 DAYS LEFT]] The first clue pops up: a locked drawer in the supply closet, a code hidden in the quarterly report. I sprint down the hallway, shoes squeaking on polished tile. The fluorescent lights flicker above me, buzzing like insects. I pry the drawer; a cold metal key clinks inside. [[SOUND – METAL CLINK]] My breath catches. The key is etched with a name: “J. Alvarez.” I remember the rumor—Alvarez vanished after a scandal. Panic rises. I slip the key into my pocket, feeling its weight like a secret weapon. Suddenly, the tablet pings. "You have ten minutes to solve the next puzzle," the manager’s voice crackles. I stare at the screen, sweat dripping down my temple. The clock ticks. I can hear a distant siren outside, growing louder. My pulse races. I type the first digit, hoping it’s right. Then. Silence. [[3 MINUTES LEFT]]

[[DAY 2 · 02:15 PM]] The stakes are higher. I have barely twelve minutes before the next challenge drops, and the live chat is spiking. My fingers tremble over the keypad. The screen flashes: "Find the hidden scandal. One wrong answer, and you’re out." I remember the key’s name—Alvarez. I dig through the digital archives, scrolling past budget sheets, HR memos, every file a potential trap. A whisper of paper rustles behind me. I turn. The manager watches from a glass wall, his smile thin. [[RULE 2 · NO LOOKING BACK]] I hear a faint beep from the speaker. A video clip plays, showing senior VP Ramirez accepting a suitcase full of cash in a dim parking lot. My stomach drops. The chat explodes. Viewers gasp. I can feel the room’s temperature drop, a chill crawling up my spine. I realize the game isn’t just about puzzles; it’s about exposing the rot. My mind races. Do I reveal the footage? If I do, Ramirez’s career ends, but the company might collapse. I glance at the timer—one minute left. My hand hovers over “upload.” The manager’s voice cuts in, "Remember, only one can win." A sudden crash echoes from the hallway; a glass door shatters. The lights flicker again. My heart slams. I press “upload.” The screen flashes green. The feed goes live. The audience watches. I hold my breath as the final seconds count down. [[COUNTDOWN 10 SECONDS]]

[[DAY 3 · 04:45 PM]] A stark white chamber, one chair, a massive screen. The manager steps forward, eyes cold. "If you survive, you get the promotion. If you fail, you’re gone." The timer reads zero. The door slams. I sit. Sweat soaks my shirt. The screen flashes the first question: "What do you do with the evidence you just aired?" I could delete it, save myself, or keep it up and watch the fallout. The distant whir of a printer echoes, like my resignation printing itself. Ozone tastes sharp. My phone vibrates—an anonymous tip: "Don’t let them win." I stare at the camera, see my colleagues’ terrified faces. I inhale. I click "keep live." The feed stays. The scandal spreads like wildfire. Alerts ping across the office; phones ring nonstop. The manager’s smile cracks. Suddenly, lights go out. A red emergency light blinks, bathing the room in blood red. A voice over the intercom: "Game over. You win, but at what cost?" Footsteps pound on tile. The door creaks. A silhouette enters, envelope in hand. The envelope is my termination notice. I realize the promotion was a ruse. The game was never about survival—it was about sacrifice. I grip the chair’s edge, heart pounding. The camera zooms in on my face. The room hums. I whisper into the silence, "Did I betray them or protect them?" The timer ticks. The final moment is a breath. I breathe. I hold my decision. The screen flashes one last line: "So… was I wrong to sabotage the game to protect my coworkers?" #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #office #ethics

premise.hook: My new manager announced a “secret project” that will give the winner a promotion—if they survive the week.
premise.twist: The project is a live‑streamed escape‑room where each task reveals a hidden scandal about senior staff, and the loser gets fired on the spot.
premise.debate: Comments will split on the ethics of gamifying employment, the fairness of public humiliation, and whether the narrator should sabotage the game to protect colleagues.
